title: procurement-approval-privacy-gov-liaison-sync
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Vanguard through procurement readiness: MSA redline scope, DPA clauses for processor/subprocessor, SOC2 evidence and KMS flow, private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), and pricing path for a 3-month pilot. Customer clarified procurement gating criteria (data classification, escrow, SLA uptime, egress fees). Agreed next steps: send MSA/DPA redlines, security pack, draft pilot SOW, and schedule legal review for next Tuesday.
topics: Pricing for pilot and reserved capacity
action_items: Alex Rivera: Share MSA annotated redline and DPA checklist (due: 2026-04-09)
Samir Patel: Export example private-deploy topology + network egress matrix (due: 2026-04-10)
Priya Nair: Provide vendor scoring template and required legal clauses (due: 2026-04-13)
Eva Li: Share SOC 2 questions + specific audit window needed (due: 2026-04-09)
Jamal Ortiz: Confirm procurement review meeting time (due: 2026-04-08)
next_steps: Redwood to send MSA redline + security pack + pilot SOW
Schedule legal-only review with Vanguard legal (Priya) next Tuesday 11am ET
Customer to run vendor scoring and send required clause list
Agree pilot success criteria and SLA targets before PO
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-06 09:00 PT | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Priya (Vanguard Legal), Jamal (Procurement), Eva (InfoSec), Marta (Platform), Omar (Vendor Risk)

[00:00] Alex Rivera: hey everyone thanks for joining this is Alex from Redwood very excited to, um, get through procurement readiness and make sure we surface the right stuff for legal and infosec. quick roll call?

[00:12] Priya Nair: Priya here from legal, hi all.

[00:15] Jamal Ortiz: Jamal, procurement.

[00:18] Eva Li: Eva, InfoSec.

[00:21] Marta Gomez: Marta, platform engineering.

[00:25] Alex Rivera: cool, thanks. Samir on the call too, our SE, will cover the private deployment options and KMS flows. Roxie from CS is here but she will be quiet.

[00:35] Samir Patel: hi everyone. quick agenda: 1) MSA/DPA redlines and which items typically block procurement 2) security artifacts and SOC2/KMS questions 3) pilot pricing and SLA expectations 4) open Qs and next steps.

[01:02] Jamal Ortiz: the procurement committee wants to make sure vendor can handle eu data, has a clear egress-fee stance, and supports an escape plan with data handoff — that's non-negotiable. also we score vendors for privileged keying, any third-party HSM is considered high risk.

[01:27] Priya Nair: from legal side we will flag any DPA clauses where subprocessors aren't listed up front — we need a subprocessors appendix or an automatic notice period. also termination assistance — how long do you retain customer data post-termination?

[01:48] Alex Rivera: understood. standard for Redwood is 90 days retention after termination for hosted by default, with options for immediate purge on request in Private deployments; we can note that in the DPA. subprocessors: we maintain a catalog and send notices 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor — we can add that clause.

[02:12] Eva Li: SOC2 is table stakes. we also need specifics on endpoint encryption, key ownership, and whether you support customer-managed keys via our KMS or using your HSM. we prefer customer-managed keys for models that touch PHI.

[02:34] Samir Patel: technically we support customer-managed keys in both Redwood Dedicated and Private. For Hosted API we offer an HSM-backed KMS integration; for VPC/private option we can have your KMS in front of the inference runtime — so keys never leave your control. bracket, caveat, there's some work on the ops side to set up key rotations and IAM roles.

[03:05] Marta Gomez: that last part, ops work, translates to network peering and firewall rules — do you have a standard topology we can review? we need to validate egress paths for data residency.

[03:25] Samir Patel: yes, I'll share an exported topology and an egress matrix. we have two reference designs: 1) VPC-connected private control plane (customer subnet with peering), 2) air-gapped on-prem pack with an optional sync agent. both have different egress models.

[03:48] Omar Khan: vendor risk: do you provide independent penetration test reports or a bug bounty summary? we also need to know whether you use any third-party telemetry or analytics SDKs, even in minimal form.

[04:05] Alex Rivera: we can provide SOC2 Type II, an SOC2 summary, and a penetration test report redacted for sensitive info. we also can provide third-party list — we try to minimize telemetry by default and can disable optional analytics for enterprise customers.

[04:28] Priya Nair: pricing — procurement wants a clear pilot path. we usually need a capped spend for the POC and a defined way to convert to committed reserved capacity. can you outline that?

[04:45] Alex Rivera: for pilots we typically propose a 3-month pilot with a usage cap and a transition playbook: if you convert within 30 days after pilot end, credits apply toward reserved capacity, and we define an expected SLO during the pilot. pricing sheet will show on-demand vs reserved delta.

[05:08] Jamal Ortiz: is there an early-termination fee in reserved capacity agreements? sometimes that's a sticking point.

[05:16] Alex Rivera: we do have pro-rated termination terms; enterprise deals can negotiate carve-outs. will put the termination economics in the SOW so procurement can score it.

[05:33] Eva Li: SLA — what is your uptime target and how do credits work? we need an objective metric and transparency in monitoring.

[05:42] Samir Patel: our Dedicated tier has a target 99.9% availability for inference endpoints; hosted tiers are in the same ballpark but can vary by model. credits are pro-rated based on token throughput; we can supply token-level trace logs via the console for audit.

[06:10] Priya Nair: token-level logs are fine as long as they don't include customer PII. also audit logs need to be immutable and exportable for 6 months.

[06:24] Alex Rivera: yes, audit logs are immutable and exportable; retention windows can be extended as a paid add-on.

[06:38] Marta Gomez: about data classification: we have three classes for this project — public, internal, and restricted (includes customer PII). The default pilot will hit internal and restricted. how do you isolate restricted requests?

[06:55] Samir Patel: for restricted we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC and customer-managed keys; that ensures network isolation, separate GPU pools, and SOC2 controls. hosted is possible but requires additional DPA controls and contractual guarantees.

[07:22] Omar Khan: subprocessors again — any plan to use third-party model optimization services? that can impact approval.

[07:33] Alex Rivera: generally we run most compilation and kernel selection in-house. for certain quantization tooling we may use vetted OSS or partners but we'd list them and they would be covered under the DPA subprocessors appendix.

[07:50] Priya Nair: good, we'll need that appendix. also, escrow — we have a requirement to have a data escrow arrangement in case of vendor insolvency for critical services. do you support that?

[08:03] Alex Rivera: yes, we support escrow for model artifacts and customer data exports; details depend on the tier and escrow provider, but we can add a clause and sample escrow MTAs.

[08:22] Jamal Ortiz: what about export controls and data transfer to other jurisdictions? EU data residency is important for us.

[08:33] Samir Patel: we have region pinning and can restrict inference to EU regions for EU customers; cross-region replication is opt-in. for export controls, we have a compliance packet and can add contractual restrictions.

[08:50] Priya Nair: for the DPA we will want specific language on subprocessors, notification timing, data retention after termination, and a right to audit for critical subsystems.

[09:05] Alex Rivera: understood. we'll propose specific wording: 30-day notice for subprocessors, 90 days retention by default, immediate purge on request for Private; allow for customer-led audit with NDA and a notice period.

[09:22] Eva Li: regarding KMS: are key rotation logs available to customers? if keys are customer-managed, we need to tie rotation events to request logs for forensic timelines.

[09:35] Samir Patel: yes, rotation events can be logged and correlated with token request traces; we'll share a sample mapping in the security pack.

[09:48] Marta Gomez: network-wise, what ports and egress hosts should our firewall team expect to open? we need a minimal list.

[09:58] Samir Patel: minimal outbound to Redwood control plane on specific IP ranges and TLS ports (we'll produce an IP list and FQDNs). for private peerings it's zero egress across public internet except the control plane endpoints.

[10:20] Priya Nair: one more legal note — indemnity caps and IP assignment for derivative outputs. we need clarity on whether Redwood asserts any ownership of generated content.

[10:36] Alex Rivera: Redwood does not claim ownership of customer-generated outputs. indemnity clauses can be discussed; standard enterprise agreements have carve-outs, we can surface language in the MSA redline.

[10:52] Jamal Ortiz: procurement also wants to see SLAs for escalation/resolution times for high-severity incidents (on-call contacts).

[10:59] Alex Rivera: we provide escalation contacts in enterprise plans, with on-call 24/7 for Sev1s, and typical response/restore SLAs in the SOW.

[11:14] Priya Nair: ok let's recap what we need from Redwood to move procurement forward.

[11:20] Samir Patel: list: 1) annotated MSA redline 2) DPA with subprocessors appendix 3) security pack (SOC2, pen test summary, KMS topology, audit log sample) 4) pilot SOW with capped spend and SLA table 5) private deployment topology + egress matrix

[11:40] Alex Rivera: yep we'll send all of that. timeline — we can have the MSA redline and security pack out within three business days. Samir will send the topology and egress matrix within four.

[11:54] Priya Nair: legal prefers the MSA redline first so we can start feeding it into our tracker. can you get it by Friday?

[12:02] Alex Rivera: yes, Friday delivery is fine.

[12:06] Jamal Ortiz: procurement will review and get back with scoring; we'll tentatively schedule a legal-only review next Tuesday at 11am ET.

[12:15] Priya Nair: yes that works, I'll invite people.

[12:19] Omar Khan: quick question — in the pilot, can you restrict telemetry and analytics? we need to ensure no usage telemetry goes to third parties.

[12:28] Samir Patel: yes, telemetry can be disabled or routed to an enterprise analytics endpoint; will include options in the security pack.

[12:40] Alex Rivera: ok, if there are no more big blockers, we'll close with action items.

[12:44] Priya Nair: just one ask: include a sample termination data export and schema so our side can validate ingestion.

[12:51] Alex Rivera: noted. Samir will attach the export schema.

[12:55] Alex Rivera: final recap: Redwood sends MSA/DPA redlines + security pack + pilot SOW by Friday; Samir sends topology and egress matrix by Monday; Vanguard schedules legal-only review Tues 11am ET; customer will share vendor scoring doc and required clauses. Thanks everyone.

[13:12] Meeting end.
